headline: Strong overnight recovery; keep the planned rest day
summary: Last night's recovery was the strongest since the marathon: 8h 26m sleep, sleeping heart rate 61 bpm, overnight HRV 51 ms, Body Battery 97 on waking, and Training Readiness 72. Yesterday's 2.40 km recovery run was appropriately short and no further workout was recorded, so the prescription was followed. Keep today as a rest day to absorb the first recovery week before resuming the four-run plan tomorrow.

recovery.label: Sleep
recovery.context: Good and 34 minutes short of Garmin's elevated 9h need. REM was 1h 55m; deep sleep was 1h 08m.

recovery.label: Sleeping HR
recovery.context: 4.6 bpm below the prior 7-night average (65.6) and 3.3 bpm below the prior 14-night average (64.3). This reverses yesterday's temporary rise to 69 bpm.

recovery.label: Resting HR
recovery.context: 3 bpm below Garmin's seven-day average of 58.

recovery.label: HRV
recovery.context: Above Garmin's 45 ms weekly average; HRV status remains balanced.

recovery.label: Body Battery
recovery.context: Garmin recorded a 92-point overnight gain; latest value was 88 at about 7:57 am.

recovery.label: Training Readiness
recovery.context: Good sleep, near-zero recovery time, and strong HRV support readiness; Garmin still rates recent sleep history poor.

recovery.label: Stress
recovery.context: Low but an incomplete morning value; overnight sleep stress averaged 9 and was rated excellent.

yesterday.title: Short recovery run followed
yesterday.summary: The prior brief accepted the already-completed 2.40 km recovery run and instructed no more running. Garmin recorded that one short run and no additional workout.
yesterday.prescribed: Stop after the 2.40 km easy run; no second run, hills, strides, tempo, or additional distance. Optional gentle walking or mobility only.
yesterday.completed: One 2.40 km recovery run in 15m 52s at 6:37/km, average HR 134, training load 30, aerobic effect 2.1, anaerobic effect 0; no additional workout.
yesterday.adherence_assessment: You followed the measurable prescription. The run remained short and easy, and no later structured training was recorded.
adherence_evidence: Completed duration was 15m 52s and distance was 2.40 km.
Average pace was 6:37/km and average heart rate was 134 bpm.
Training load was 30 with aerobic effect 2.1, anaerobic effect 0, and Garmin labelled the session recovery.
No second Garmin activity was recorded on 6 September.
adherence_caveats: Garmin cannot verify perceived effort, pain, illness, exact terrain, or unrecorded walking and mobility.
The absence of a second recorded workout does not prove complete inactivity after the run.

environment.humidity_dew_point_context: Reliable route-time humidity and dew point were unavailable.
environment.heat_impact_interpretation: The temperature range alone does not show material heat strain; the controlled pace, heart rate, and training effect are consistent with an easy recovery effort.
environment.limitations: Watch temperature can be influenced by body heat and sun exposure, and the range is not equivalent to route-level air temperature.

recommendation.title: Rest today
details: No running today. Preserve the Monday rest day from the weekly recovery plan.
Optional: 20–30 minutes of easy walking or 10–15 minutes of gentle mobility, RPE 1–2.
Sydney is mild today at roughly 13–22°C, so heat is not a limiting factor. Good conditions do not create a need to add training.
If tomorrow's overnight record remains reassuring, proceed with the planned 5 km easy run.
recommendation.alternative: Complete rest is fully appropriate and preferred if you feel any residual marathon soreness or unusual fatigue.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop optional activity for pain, illness, dizziness, altered gait, unusual fatigue, or other concerning symptoms. Symptoms and medical advice override Garmin scores.

signals.label: Overnight rebound
signals.interpretation: Sleep duration and overnight recharge improved sharply and now support normal daily function.

signals.label: Autonomic recovery
signals.interpretation: Sleeping HR fell below both recent baselines while HRV rose above its weekly average, a reassuring combination.

signals.label: Post-marathon load
signals.interpretation: Training load is now low. The correct response is gradual rebuilding, beginning after today's planned rest rather than adding an unscheduled session.

signals.label: Rolling seven days
signals.interpretation: Both runs were short aerobic-base or recovery sessions. The very low total reflects deliberate post-marathon recovery.

caveats: Garmin's sleep stages and heart-rate measures are wearable-derived; interpret trends alongside how you feel.
Today's stress, Body Battery, and readiness values are incomplete morning measures.
The weekly sleeping-HR comparisons exclude the current night and use the available prior seven and fourteen valid nights.
Sydney weather is city-level context, not route-level measurement.

run_assessments.title: 6 September recovery run
run_assessments.summary: 2.40 km in 15m 52s (6:37/km), average HR 134, training load 30, aerobic effect 2.1, anaerobic effect 0.
run_assessments.interpretation: The session matched a recovery purpose and no additional training was recorded. Garmin's 18–28°C temperature range does not establish meaningful heat strain; perceived effort and terrain remain unobservable.
